content: The ACCORD BP trial, conducted by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), demonstrated no significant benefit in the primary composite endpoint, which included nonfatal myocardial infarction (MI), nonfatal stroke, and cardiovascular death, when comparing intensive blood pressure control to standard control. However, intensive blood pressure control was associated with a 41% reduction in stroke risk. It is important to note that this reduction in stroke risk was not sustained during the follow-up period. Additionally, adverse effects were more frequently observed in the intensive control group. These adverse effects included elevated serum creatinine levels and abnormalities in electrolyte balance.
